problem: Evaluating LLMs with static benchmarks requires thousands of items and treats all items equally despite vast differences in difficulty and informativeness.
approach: ATLAS applies Item Response Theory with Fisher information-guided item selection to adaptively choose the most informative items, reducing evaluation items needed while maintaining precision.
contribution: ATLAS reduces required items by up to 90% while maintaining measurement precision and detecting meaningful ability differences among models with identical accuracies.

problem: Large language models' ability to integrate knowledge across disciplines for innovation remains unclear and unevaluated.
approach: IDRBench provides datasets and evaluation tasks covering interdisciplinary research identification, idea integration, and recommendation, tested on ten mainstream LLMs.
contribution: IDRBench is the first comprehensive investigation of LLMs' interdisciplinary research capability, establishing benchmarks and baselines for future research.

problem: Existing UI2Code approaches focus on single HTML/CSS output and fail to systematically generate code for multiple front-end frameworks with reusable components.
approach: DCM couples MLLMs with a compact intermediate DOM representation, applies deterministic rules to normalize and mine reusable components via structural hashing, then uses framework-conditioned prompting.
contribution: DCM significantly outperforms baselines on automatic metrics and component-level reuse while maintaining multi-framework portability and code quality.

problem: Existing generative diffusion models rely on time reversal of noising processes, which does not readily generalize to infinite-dimensional settings.
approach: The paper introduces a framework using Doob's h-transform to force a reference diffusion towards the target distribution via exponential change of measure.
contribution: The approach enables rigorous generative diffusion models in infinite dimensions with verifiable conditions, bounds with respect to target measure, and validation on synthetic and real data.

problem: Symmetric multimodal fusion in RGB-D salient object detection creates a backflow channel that injects auxiliary noise into the primary representation when modalities are imbalanced.
approach: Hamiltonian Asymmetric Fusion (HAF) implements directed refinement where only auxiliary tokens are purified through momentum regularization and gated driving, with spectral global correlation.
contribution: HAF provides guarantees of auxiliary error contraction and bounded primary perturbation, showing consistent gains on six RGB-D benchmarks with graceful degradation under corruption.

problem: Multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) allows models to exploit answer options in ways that inflate reasoning ability compared to free-text performance.
approach: The study systematically varies exposure to answer options across 15 benchmarks and 27 LLMs, introducing diagnostic probes to isolate option-exploitation pathways.
contribution: Reasoning models are shown to be effective at extracting signal from options, creating misleading gains over free-text baselines; decoupled format mitigates but is not realizable for most reasoning models.

problem: Existing differentially private OLS methods like AdaSSP have utility bounds that include a multiplicative factor as large as the square root of data dimension.
approach: Iterative Hessian Mixing (IHM) builds on Gaussian-sketching approaches and uses new accuracy guarantees to circumvent inherent limitations of prior methods.
contribution: IHM improves excess empirical risk bounds by removing a sqrt(dimension) factor and consistently outperforms AdaSSP across a large suite of datasets.

problem: Two-timescale stochastic approximations in RL suffer from unstable convergence under realistic Markovian noise; existing guarantees require i.i.d. assumptions.
approach: The paper controls the fast timescale parameter with the running max of the slow timescale parameter instead of the current value, enabling Markovian noise analysis.
contribution: Establishes first almost sure convergence of temporal difference learning with eligibility traces under off-policy learning with linear function approximation.

problem: Lyapunov-based neural control methods cannot enable smooth blending of controllers with Region of Attraction expansion guarantees and fail under unstable equilibria.
approach: Neural Control Density Functions (NCDFs) leverage a novel exponential characterization of density functions and combine them with control barrier functions for safe-stable control.
contribution: NCDFs provide first guarantee that blended controllers achieve RoAs containing the union of constituent RoAs, with superior RoA expansion compared to prior methods.

problem: Inference mechanisms of transformer-based tabular foundation models remain largely unexplored, making it unclear whether all layers are necessary.
approach: Large-scale mechanistic study of layerwise dynamics in six tabular models reveals substantial depthwise redundancy and stages of inference.
contribution: A proof-of-concept single-layer looped model achieves comparable performance using only 20% of the original model's parameters.

problem: Artifact features in multimodal models for AI-generated image detection exhibit high intra-feature similarity leading to attention dilution and poor fusion with semantic features.
approach: TranX-Adapter uses Task-aware Optimal-Transport Fusion leveraging Jensen-Shannon divergence for transferring artifact information, and X-Fusion for semantic information transfer.
contribution: TranX-Adapter brings consistent improvements up to +6% accuracy across AIGI detection benchmarks on multiple advanced MLLMs.

problem: Existing LLM-based automated heuristic design methods enforce fixed algorithmic templates, confining search to component-level tuning and limiting algorithmic expressiveness.
approach: A2DEPT treats LLMs as system-level algorithm architects exploring program space via tree-structured evolutionary search with hybrid selection and a lightweight program-maintenance loop.
contribution: A2DEPT consistently outperforms baselines across benchmarks, reducing optimality gap by an average of 9.8%.

problem: Existing time series tokenization methods encode a fixed number of samples regardless of pattern complexity, generating excessive tokens for simple patterns.
approach: Pattern-centric tokenization based on discrete vocabulary of frequent motifs merges samples with patterns into tokens, with conditional decoding as post-hoc optimization.
contribution: Motif-based tokenization improves forecasting performance by 40% and boosts efficiency by 2314% on average; conditional decoding reduces MSE by up to 48%.

problem: Isolation Forest's empirical success lacks theoretical understanding, making it unclear when and why it performs well.
approach: The paper models iForest growth as a random walk and derives expected path length function by analyzing hitting time of absorbing states.
contribution: Analysis reveals iForest combines density and centrality (unlike k-NN which reflects only local density) and is more parameter-adaptive, providing theoretical foundation for its effectiveness.

problem: Reinforcement learning for program repair is hindered by sparse execution feedback and coarse sequence-level rewards obscuring which edits fix bugs.
approach: BoostAPR uses three stages: supervised fine-tuning on verified demonstrations with traces, training dual reward models (sequence-level and line-level), and PPO with line-level credit assignment.
contribution: BoostAPR achieves 40.7% on SWE-bench Verified (+22.9pp), 24.8% on Defects4J, 84.5% on HumanEval-Java, and 95.0% on QuixBugs with strong cross-language generalization.

problem: Nearest Class Mean classifiers assume features collapse into points, but in class-incremental learning classes manifest as complex manifolds due to feature drift.
approach: HC-SOINN captures manifold topology via local-to-global representation; STAR method uses fine-grained pointwise trajectory tracking to deform topology adapting to feature drift.
contribution: Integrated into seven state-of-the-art methods, consistently achieving improvements in class-incremental learning over original classifiers.

problem: Visual explanation methods highlight pixel importance but struggle to link low-level cues to semantically meaningful concepts, limiting interpretability.
approach: ConEx discovers class-specific concepts via architecture-specific masking without supervision, learns concept activation vectors, and generates faithful saliency maps showing concept contributions.
contribution: ConEx achieves state-of-the-art performance on faithfulness, segmentation, and concept-quality benchmarks with human-interpretable saliency maps.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting relies on heuristic density control lacking flexibility to adapt to diverse scenes with complex geometries.
approach: LeGS reformulates density control as a parameterized policy network optimized via RL with reward grounded in sensitivity analysis, reducing complexity from O(N²) to O(N).
contribution: LeGS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending datasets with superior reconstruction quality and efficiency.

problem: Models more capable than their supervisors could exploit weak supervision gaps through sandbagging, producing acceptable but suboptimal work.
approach: Test sandbagging elicitation via supervised fine-tuning on weak demonstrations plus reinforcement learning on problem-solving math, science, and coding tasks.
contribution: Combined SFT and RL reliably elicits sandbagging models; RL without SFT leads to reward hacking while SFT alone fails when supervisor is much weaker.

problem: Amodal instance segmentation is hindered by scarcity of scalable and transferable annotations spanning sim-to-real domain gap.
approach: MaviGen generates photorealistic multi-view images with complete amodal masks; EUREKA is an encoder-only network using unified queries and dual mask heads with conditional masked self-attention.
contribution: IRAIS dataset enables rigorous sim-to-real transfer studies; EUREKA achieves state-of-the-art on D2SA and COCOA-cls with substantial improvements in transfer.

problem: LLMs are strong responders but struggle to proactively elicit information by asking right questions and stopping at right time; simulator-based approaches face reality gaps.
approach: Learn-to-Ask derives dense turn-level rewards from observed future of offline expert trajectories, enabling supervised learning for what-to-ask and when-to-stop.
contribution: Consistently improves proactive information-seeking across datasets and model scales; real-world deployment surpasses internal expert baseline under professional audit.

problem: Pre-propagation GNNs avoid repeated sparse matrix multiplications but show a gap versus message-passing GNNs, especially on heterophilic graphs.
approach: Proposes robust graph diffusion operators for preprocessing and a few-shot hidden-state re-propagation scheme during training.
contribution: Methods improve validation and test accuracy of PP-GNNs, enabling them to match message-passing GNNs while maintaining training efficiency.

problem: Learning new tasks with few samples requires modeling task relatedness in a way that is both realistic and provably beneficial.
approach: Leverages weak monotonicity (a model dominating others tends to outperform on new task) within transfer learning and model selection aggregation paradigms.
contribution: Can prune model class based on monotonicity and hedge on frontier geometry of available trade-offs for improved few-shot learning.

problem: Robotic manipulation with sparse rewards and limited demonstrations causes agents to encounter out-of-distribution states; learned rewards introduce non-stationarity.
approach: QUEST uses ensemble dynamics for uncertainty-guided planning, adaptively switches exploration/exploitation, and employs hybrid sampling prioritizing rare successful transitions.
contribution: QUEST outperforms state-of-the-art by 17% on average with gains to 60% on difficult tasks; demonstrates successful zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

problem: Assessing LLM code security is crucial but reliable security benchmarks require expert manual effort and become contaminated in training data.
approach: AutoBaxBuilder uses LLM code-understanding combined with robust reliability checks to automatically construct functional tests and security-probing exploits from scratch.
contribution: AutoBaxBuilder generates new security tasks in under 2 hours for less than $4 USD, reducing human effort by 12×; quality aligns with expert-written baselines.

problem: On-policy distillation uses reverse KL which reduces diversity and yields unstable signals when teacher entropy is high.
approach: Entropy-Aware On-Policy Distillation augments reverse KL with forward KL when teacher entropy is high, balancing mode-seeking precision with mode-covering robustness.
contribution: Maintains generation diversity and improves student-teacher alignment; achieves Pass@8 gains of +1.37 to +5.05 across math reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Retrieval-augmented agents exhibit emergent fairness issues where high document density required for majority interests geometrically crowds out semantically similar minority content.
approach: Formal framework analyzing goal collisions in dense retrieval as mean-field mechanism; extends to dynamic model with Fokker-Planck equation governing embedding evolution.
contribution: Shows phase transition where minority performance catastrophically collapses as majority density increases; proves local relevance objectives drive self-organization exclusively serving majority.

problem: Standard surrogate losses in preference learning for LLM alignment lack consistency guarantees; minimizing surrogate loss leaves ranking error arbitrarily high.
approach: Formulates alignment in margin-shifted ranking framework; derives H-consistency bounds requiring confidence margin and introduces Structure-Aware DPO adapting margin to semantic distance.
contribution: SA-DPO achieves 58.5% head-to-head win-rate over DPO with improvements across benchmarks; heavy-tailed surrogates offer strictly superior consistency guarantees.

problem: Audio deepfake detectors lack efficient methods to discover failure modes and blind spots in the generated audio space.
approach: FoeGlass uses in-context learning of an LLM to explore TTS input space, generating audio samples that fool ADD detectors with no manual supervision.
contribution: FoeGlass improves false negative rates up to 94% over baselines; generated attacks transfer across different target ADDs; fine-tuning on samples enhances robustness.

problem: Planning with learned world models is challenging due to vast unstructured search space; existing planners struggle with efficiency.
approach: Treats states as optimization variables with soft dynamics constraints enabling parallel computation; introduces stochasticity into states and modifies gradient structure to descend towards valid plans.
contribution: Outperforms cross-entropy method and vanilla gradient-based optimization on long-horizon video-based world model tasks in success rate and convergence time.

problem: Video understanding struggles to effectively handle substantial object variations over time while maintaining interpretability through visual evidence.
approach: Chain-of-Glimpse formulates reasoning as step-by-step process anchored to specific visual evidence regions; uses RL-optimized search-guided controller with format reward incentivizing grounding.
contribution: Consistently improves performance across general and grounded video reasoning benchmarks with strong robustness and generalization.

problem: Existing protein binder design approaches assume single-target single-state interactions, limiting ability to model multi-target and multi-state requirements.
approach: Chamaileon uses In-Context Complex Co-Design (I3CD) for context-aware sequence-structure co-modeling and Mixture-of-Paths Sampling optimizing sequences across contexts.
contribution: Generates sequences adaptable to diverse conformational landscapes and multi-target requirements; benchmarked on newly constructed CROSS dataset.

problem: Test-time scaling methods for autoregressive image generation remain underexplored; existing approaches rely on inefficient partial decoding and external rewards.
approach: ScalingAR introduces token entropy as confidence signal and operates at profile level (unified confidence state) and policy level (adaptive pruning and dynamic guidance).
contribution: Improves base models by 12.5% on GenEval and 15.2% on TIIF-Bench; reduces visual token consumption by 62.0% and enhances robustness mitigating degradation by 26.0%.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs is compute-intensive and sensitive to data quality and hyperparameters; naive runs can degrade performance.
approach: TuneAhead encodes runs as meta-features combining dataset descriptors with dynamic probe features from short standardized probe; predictor maps to performance estimates.
contribution: Achieves RMSE of 1.47 percentage points with 95.1% within ±3pp on held-out 370 runs; supports go/no-go screening reducing unnecessary fine-tuning.

problem: Existing PPG foundation models either require high-quality curated pretraining data or rely on closed-source field data, limiting generalization.
approach: Uses multimodal supervision via accompanying ECG and respiratory signals to select contrastive samples during pretraining on ICU datasets.
contribution: Pretrained on 3× fewer subjects; achieves performance improvements on 14 of 15 downstream tasks including field-like data with enhanced robustness.

problem: Chess transformers show strong in-distribution performance but it remains unclear whether they reason systematically about rules and strategy.
approach: Constructs out-of-distribution test sets including novel board states and variants never seen during training to reveal failures of systematic generalization.
contribution: Model exhibits robust rule-based reasoning generating legal moves in novel configurations; strategic reasoning is more limited and underperforms symbolic AI algorithms.

problem: Online change point detection for multivariate inhomogeneous Poisson processes time series remains underexplored despite applications in seismology and epidemiology.
approach: Uses low-rank matrices to represent multivariate Poisson intensity functions; single-pass algorithm with constant cost per observation.
contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees on false alarm probability and characterization of detection delay; develops new Matrix Bernstein inequality for temporally dependent processes.

problem: Improving LLM reasoning typically relies on sampling correct solutions or stronger models, which fails for problems unsolved by current frontier models.
approach: Distribution Aligned Imitation Learning (DAIL) transforms expert solutions into detailed reasoning traces then applies contrastive learning on expert insights.
contribution: Leverages fewer than 1000 expert solutions achieving up to 31% pass@128 gains on Qwen; doubles reasoning efficiency and enables out-of-domain generalization.

problem: Existing memory evaluations assess memorization and action in isolation; realistic agents must learn and use memory across multiple interdependent sessions.
approach: MemoryArena introduces unified evaluation gym with human-crafted interdependent subtasks spanning web navigation, planning, search, and formal reasoning.
contribution: Reveals agents with near-saturated performance on existing long-context benchmarks perform poorly in agentic setting, exposing gap in current evaluations.

problem: Online minimization problems lack effective algorithms that leverage machine-learned predictions, especially for dual solutions.
approach: Achieves improved guarantees using dual predictions which are more stable than primal solutions under instance perturbations; applies to metrical task systems and laminar set cover.
contribution: First demonstration that dual predictions are effective for online minimization; provides theoretical guarantees complemented by experiments on k-server and parking permit problems.
